passages.text: Later, King Belshazzar held a great feast for a thousand of his nobles, and he drank wine with them.
passages.sermon:
King Belshazzar was the ruler of Babylon.
He held a great feast.
He invited a thousand of his nobles.
He drank wine with his nobles.
passages.original: בֵּלְשַׁאצַּ֣ר מַלְכָּ֗א עֲבַד֙ לְחֶ֣ם רַ֔ב לְרַבְרְבָנ֖וֹהִי אֲלַ֑ף וְלָקֳבֵ֥ל אַלְפָּ֖א חַמְרָ֥א שָׁתֵֽה׃

passages.text: Under the influence of the wine, Belshazzar gave orders to bring in the gold and silver vessels that Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken from the temple in Jerusalem, so that the king could drink from them, along with his nobles, his wives, and his concubines.
passages.sermon:
Belshazzar was the king of Babylon.
Belshazzar drank wine at a feast.
The wine influenced Belshazzar.
Belshazzar gave an order.
He told his servants to bring gold and silver vessels.
Nebuchadnezzar was Belshazzar’s father.
Nebuchadnezzar had taken these vessels from the temple in Jerusalem.
Belshazzar wanted to use these vessels at the feast.
Belshazzar planned to drink from them.
His nobles would also drink from them.
His wives would drink from them.
His concubines would drink from them.
passages.original: בֵּלְשַׁאצַּ֞ר אֲמַ֣ר׀ בִּטְעֵ֣ם חַמְרָ֗א לְהַיְתָיָה֙ לְמָאנֵי֙ דַּהֲבָ֣א וְכַסְפָּ֔א דִּ֤י הַנְפֵּק֙ נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֣ר אֲב֔וּהִי מִן־ הֵיכְלָ֖א דִּ֣י בִירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וְיִשְׁתּ֣וֹן בְּה֗וֹן מַלְכָּא֙ וְרַבְרְבָנ֔וֹהִי שֵׁגְלָתֵ֖הּ וּלְחֵנָתֵֽהּ׃

passages.text: Thus they brought in the gold vessels that had been taken from the temple, the house of God in Jerusalem, and the king drank from them, along with his nobles, his wives, and his concubines.
passages.sermon:
King Belshazzar ruled Babylon.
He held a great feast for his nobles.
He ordered his servants to bring gold vessels.
Nebuchadnezzar, his father, had taken these vessels from the temple in Jerusalem.
The temple in Jerusalem was the house of God.
The servants brought the gold vessels into the feast.
The king drank from the gold vessels.
His nobles drank from them.
His wives drank from them.
His concubines drank from them.
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֗יִן הַיְתִיו֙ מָאנֵ֣י דַהֲבָ֔א דִּ֣י הַנְפִּ֗קוּ מִן־ הֵֽיכְלָ֛א דִּֽי־ בֵ֥ית אֱלָהָ֖א דִּ֣י בִירֽוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וְאִשְׁתִּ֣יו בְּה֗וֹן מַלְכָּא֙ וְרַבְרְבָנ֔וֹהִי שֵׁגְלָתֵ֖הּ וּלְחֵנָתֵֽהּ׃

passages.text: As they drank the wine, they praised their gods of gold and silver, bronze and iron, wood and stone.
passages.sermon:
Belshazzar was the king of Babylon.
He drank wine with his nobles, his wives, and his concubines.
They used gold and silver vessels from the temple of God in Jerusalem.
As they drank the wine, they praised their gods.
They praised gods made of gold.
They praised gods made of silver.
They praised gods made of bronze.
They praised gods made of iron.
They praised gods made of wood.
They praised gods made of stone.
passages.original: אִשְׁתִּ֖יו חַמְרָ֑א וְ֠שַׁבַּחוּ לֵֽאלָהֵ֞י דַּהֲבָ֧א וְכַסְפָּ֛א נְחָשָׁ֥א פַרְזְלָ֖א אָעָ֥א וְאַבְנָֽא׃

passages.text: At that moment the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall, near the lampstand in the royal palace. As the king watched the hand that was writing, his face grew pale and his thoughts so alarmed him that his hips gave way and his knees knocked together.
passages.sermon:
King Belshazzar was in the royal palace.
He saw something strange happen.
The fingers of a human hand appeared.
The fingers wrote on the plaster of the wall.
The writing was near the lampstand.
The king watched the hand as it wrote.
The king’s face became pale.
The king felt very afraid.
His thoughts troubled him deeply.
His hips became weak.
His knees knocked together.
passages.original: בַּהּ־ שַׁעֲתָ֗ה נְפַקוּ אֶצְבְּעָן֙ דִּ֣י יַד־ אֱנָ֔שׁ וְכָֽתְבָן֙ לָקֳבֵ֣ל נֶבְרַשְׁתָּ֔א עַל־ גִּירָ֕א דִּֽי־ כְתַ֥ל הֵיכְלָ֖א דִּ֣י מַלְכָּ֑א וּמַלְכָּ֣א חָזֵ֔ה פַּ֥ס יְדָ֖ה דִּ֥י כָתְבָֽה׃ אֱדַ֤יִן מַלְכָּא֙ זִיוֺ֣הִי שְׁנ֔וֹהִי וְרַעיֹנֹ֖הִי יְבַהֲלוּנֵּ֑הּ וְקִטְרֵ֤י חַרְצֵהּ֙ מִשְׁתָּרַ֔יִן וְאַ֨רְכֻבָּתֵ֔הּ דָּ֥א לְדָ֖א נָֽקְשָֽׁן׃

passages.text: The king called out for the enchanters, astrologers, and diviners to be brought in, and he said to these wise men of Babylon, “Whoever reads this inscription and tells me its interpretation will be clothed in purple and have a gold chain placed around his neck, and he will be made the third highest ruler in the kingdom.”
passages.sermon:
King Belshazzar was afraid.
He called loudly for his wise men.
He wanted the enchanters, astrologers, and diviners to come in.
These men were known for their wisdom in Babylon.
The king spoke to them.
He said, “Whoever can read this writing and explain its meaning to me will receive a great reward.
He will wear purple clothes.
He will have a gold chain around his neck.
He will become the third highest ruler in the kingdom.”
passages.original: קָרֵ֤א מַלְכָּא֙ בְּחַ֔יִל לְהֶֽעָלָה֙ לְאָ֣שְׁפַיָּ֔א כַּשְׂדָּיֵא וְגָזְרַיָּ֑א עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֣ר׀ לְחַכִּימֵ֣י בָבֶ֗ל דִּ֣י כָל־ אֱ֠נָשׁ דִּֽי־ יִקְרֵ֞ה כְּתָבָ֣ה דְנָ֗ה וּפִשְׁרֵהּ֙ יְחַוִּנַּ֔נִי אַרְגְּוָנָ֣א יִלְבַּ֗שׁ וְהַמּוֹנְכָא דִֽי־ דַהֲבָא֙ עַֽל־ צַוְּארֵ֔הּ וְתַלְתִּ֥י בְמַלְכוּתָ֖א יִשְׁלַֽט׃ס

passages.text: So all the king’s wise men came in, but they could not read the inscription or interpret it for him.
passages.sermon:
All the wise men of the king entered the room.
They tried to help the king.
They saw the writing on the wall.
They could not read the inscription.
They could not tell the king what it meant.
passages.original: אֱדַ֙יִן֙ עָלֲלִין כֹּ֖ל חַכִּימֵ֣י מַלְכָּ֑א וְלָֽא־ כָהֲלִ֤ין כְּתָבָא֙ לְמִקְרֵ֔א וּפִשְׁרָא לְהוֹדָעָ֥ה לְמַלְכָּֽא׃

passages.text: Then King Belshazzar became even more terrified, his face grew even more pale, and his nobles were bewildered.
passages.sermon:
King Belshazzar was the ruler of Babylon.
He became very afraid.
His face turned pale.
His nobles were confused.
passages.original: אֱ֠דַיִן מַלְכָּ֤א בֵלְשַׁאצַּר֙ שַׂגִּ֣יא מִתְבָּהַ֔ל וְזִיוֺ֖הִי שָׁנַ֣יִן עֲל֑וֹהִי וְרַבְרְבָנ֖וֹהִי מִֽשְׁתַּבְּשִֽׁין׃

passages.text: Hearing the outcry of the king and his nobles, the queen entered the banquet hall. “O king, may you live forever!” she said. “Do not let your thoughts terrify you, or your face grow pale.
passages.sermon:
The queen heard the king and his nobles crying out.
She entered the banquet hall.
She spoke to King Belshazzar.
She said, “O king, may you live forever.”
She told him, “Do not let your thoughts terrify you.”
She also said, “Do not let your face grow pale.”
passages.original: מַלְכְּתָ֕א לָקֳבֵ֨ל מִלֵּ֤י מַלְכָּא֙ וְרַבְרְבָנ֔וֹהִי לְבֵ֥ית מִשְׁתְּיָ֖א עַלֲלַת עֲנָ֨ת מַלְכְּתָ֜א וַאֲמֶ֗רֶת מַלְכָּא֙ לְעָלְמִ֣ין חֱיִ֔י אַֽל־ יְבַהֲלוּךְ֙ רַעְיוֹנָ֔ךְ וְזִיוָ֖יךְ אַל־ יִשְׁתַּנּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods in him. In the days of your father he was found to have insight, intelligence, and wisdom like that of the gods. Your father, King Nebuchadnezzar, appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, astrologers, and diviners. Your own father, the king, did this because Daniel, the one he named Belteshazzar, was found to have an extraordinary spirit, as well as knowledge, understanding, and the ability to interpret dreams, explain riddles, and solve difficult problems. Summon Daniel, therefore, and he will give you the interpretation.”
passages.sermon:
There is a man in your kingdom.
He has the spirit of the holy gods in him.
In the days of your father, people found insight in him.
They found intelligence in him.
They found wisdom in him, like the wisdom of the gods.
Your father was King Nebuchadnezzar.
King Nebuchadnezzar appointed this man as chief over the magicians.
He made him chief over the enchanters.
He made him chief over the astrologers.
He made him chief over the diviners.
Your father did this because Daniel had an extraordinary spirit.
Daniel had knowledge.
Daniel had understanding.
Daniel could interpret dreams.
Daniel could explain riddles.
Daniel could solve difficult problems.
The king gave Daniel the name Belteshazzar.
Now call for Daniel.
He will give you the interpretation.
passages.original: אִיתַ֨י גְּבַ֜ר בְּמַלְכוּתָ֗ךְ דִּ֠י ר֣וּחַ אֱלָהִ֣ין קַדִּישִׁין֮ בֵּהּ֒ וּבְיוֹמֵ֣י אֲב֗וּךְ נַהִיר֧וּ וְשָׂכְלְתָנ֛וּ וְחָכְמָ֥ה כְּחָכְמַת־ אֱלָהִ֖ין הִשְׁתְּכַ֣חַת בֵּ֑הּ וּמַלְכָּ֤א נְבֻֽכַדְנֶצַּר֙ אֲב֔וּךְ רַ֧ב חַרְטֻמִּ֣ין אָֽשְׁפִ֗ין כַּשְׂדָּאִין֙ גָּזְרִ֔ין הֲקִימֵ֖הּ אֲב֥וּךְ מַלְכָּֽא׃ כָּל־ קֳבֵ֡ל דִּ֣י ר֣וּחַ׀ יַתִּירָ֡ה וּמַנְדַּ֡ע וְשָׂכְלְתָנ֡וּ מְפַשַּׁ֣ר חֶלְמִין֩ וַֽאַֽחֲוָיַ֨ת אֲחִידָ֜ן וּמְשָׁרֵ֣א קִטְרִ֗ין הִשְׁתְּכַ֤חַת בֵּהּ֙ בְּדָ֣נִיֵּ֔אל דִּֽי־ מַלְכָּ֥א שָׂם־ שְׁמֵ֖הּ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּ֑ר כְּעַ֛ן דָּנִיֵּ֥אל יִתְקְרֵ֖י וּפִשְׁרָ֥ה יְהַֽחֲוֵֽה׃פ

passages.text: So Daniel was brought before the king, who asked him, “Are you Daniel, one of the exiles my father the king brought from Judah?
passages.sermon:
Daniel was an exile from Judah.
The king’s father brought Daniel from Judah.
The king summoned Daniel.
Daniel stood before the king.
The king spoke to Daniel.
The king asked, “Are you Daniel?”
The king said, “You are one of the exiles.”
The king said, “My father brought you from Judah.”
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֙יִן֙ דָּֽנִיֵּ֔אל הֻעַ֖ל קֳדָ֣ם מַלְכָּ֑א עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֣ר לְדָנִיֵּ֗אל אַנְתָּה ה֤וּא דָנִיֵּאל֙ דִּֽי־ מִן־ בְּנֵ֤י גָלוּתָא֙ דִּ֣י יְה֔וּד דִּ֥י הַיְתִ֛י מַלְכָּ֥א אַ֖בִי מִן־ יְהֽוּד׃

passages.text: I have heard that the spirit of the gods is in you, and that you have insight, intelligence, and extraordinary wisdom.
passages.sermon:
Daniel, you are a man from Judah.
You live in exile in Babylon.
People say the spirit of the holy gods is in you.
You have insight.
You have intelligence.
You have extraordinary wisdom.
These qualities are found in you.
passages.original: וְשִׁמְעֵ֣ת עֲלַיִךְ דִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ אֱלָהִ֖ין בָּ֑ךְ וְנַהִיר֧וּ וְשָׂכְלְתָנ֛וּ וְחָכְמָ֥ה יַתִּירָ֖ה הִשְׁתְּכַ֥חַת בָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: Now the wise men and enchanters were brought before me to read this inscription and interpret it for me, but they could not give its interpretation.
passages.sermon:
The king called the wise men and enchanters to come before him.
He asked them to read the inscription.
He wanted them to tell him what it meant.
They could not explain the meaning of the words.
They failed to give the interpretation.
passages.original: וּכְעַ֞ן הֻעַ֣לּוּ קָֽדָמַ֗י חַכִּֽימַיָּא֙ אָֽשְׁפַיָּ֔א דִּֽי־ כְתָבָ֤ה דְנָה֙ יִקְר֔וֹן וּפִשְׁרֵ֖הּ לְהוֹדָעֻתַ֑נִי וְלָֽא־ כָהֲלִ֥ין פְּשַֽׁר־ מִלְּתָ֖א לְהַחֲוָיָֽה׃

passages.text: But I have heard about you, that you are able to give interpretations and solve difficult problems. Therefore, if you can read this inscription and give me its interpretation, you will be clothed in purple and have a gold chain placed around your neck, and you will be made the third highest ruler in the kingdom.”
passages.sermon:
The king spoke to Daniel.
The king said, "I have heard about you."
People say you can explain meanings.
People say you can solve difficult problems.
Now, I have a message written here.
If you can read this writing,
and if you can tell me what it means,
I will reward you.
You will wear a purple robe.
You will have a gold chain around your neck.
You will become the third highest ruler in the kingdom.
passages.original: וַאֲנָה֙ שִׁמְעֵ֣ת עֲלַיִךְ דִּֽי־ תוּכַל פִּשְׁרִ֛ין לְמִפְשַׁ֖ר וְקִטְרִ֣ין לְמִשְׁרֵ֑א כְּעַ֡ן הֵן֩ תּוּכַל כְּתָבָ֜א לְמִקְרֵ֗א וּפִשְׁרֵהּ֙ לְהוֹדָ֣עֻתַ֔נִי אַרְגְּוָנָ֣א תִלְבַּ֗שׁ וְהַמּוֹנְכָא דִֽי־ דַהֲבָא֙ עַֽל־ צַוְּארָ֔ךְ וְתַלְתָּ֥א בְמַלְכוּתָ֖א תִּשְׁלַֽט׃פ

passages.text: In response, Daniel said to the king, “You may keep your gifts for yourself and give your rewards to someone else. Nevertheless, I will read the inscription for the king and interpret it for him.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a prophet of God.
Daniel stood before the king.
Daniel answered the king.
Daniel said, “Keep your gifts for yourself.
Give your rewards to someone else.
I will read the inscription for you, O king.
I will tell you its meaning.”
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֜יִן עָנֵ֣ה דָנִיֵּ֗אל וְאָמַר֙ קֳדָ֣ם מַלְכָּ֔א מַתְּנָתָךְ֙ לָ֣ךְ לֶֽהֶוְיָ֔ן וּנְבָ֥זְבְּיָתָ֖ךְ לְאָחֳרָ֣ן הַ֑ב בְּרַ֗ם כְּתָבָא֙ אֶקְרֵ֣א לְמַלְכָּ֔א וּפִשְׁרָ֖א אֲהוֹדְעִנֵּֽהּ׃

passages.text: As for you, O king, the Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar sovereignty and greatness, glory and honor.
passages.sermon:
O king, I speak to you now.
The Most High God is the one true God.
He gave your father Nebuchadnezzar power.
He gave him a great kingdom.
He gave him glory.
He gave him honor.
passages.original: אַנְתָּה מַלְכָּ֑א אֱלָהָא֙ עִלָּיָא מַלְכוּתָ֤א וּרְבוּתָא֙ וִיקָרָ֣א וְהַדְרָ֔ה יְהַ֖ב לִנְבֻכַדְנֶצַּ֥ר אֲבֽוּךְ׃

passages.text: Because of the greatness that He bestowed on him, the people of every nation and language trembled in fear before him. He killed whom he wished and kept alive whom he wished; he exalted whom he wished and humbled whom he wished.
passages.sermon:
God gave Nebuchadnezzar great power.
God made Nebuchadnezzar great among all people.
People from every nation feared Nebuchadnezzar.
People who spoke every language trembled before Nebuchadnezzar.
Nebuchadnezzar killed anyone he wanted.
Nebuchadnezzar let live anyone he wanted.
Nebuchadnezzar honored anyone he wanted.
Nebuchadnezzar humbled anyone he wanted.
passages.original: וּמִן־ רְבוּתָא֙ דִּ֣י יְהַב־ לֵ֔הּ כֹּ֣ל עַֽמְמַיָּ֗א אֻמַיָּא֙ וְלִשָּׁ֣נַיָּ֔א הֲו֛וֹ זָאֲעִין וְדָחֲלִ֖ין מִן־ קֳדָמ֑וֹהִי דִּֽי־ הֲוָ֨ה צָבֵ֜א הֲוָ֣א קָטֵ֗ל וְדִֽי־ הֲוָ֤ה צָבֵא֙ הֲוָ֣ה מַחֵ֔א וְדִֽי־ הֲוָ֤ה צָבֵא֙ הֲוָ֣ה מָרִ֔ים וְדִֽי־ הֲוָ֥ה צָבֵ֖א הֲוָ֥ה מַשְׁפִּֽיל׃

passages.text: But when his heart became arrogant and his spirit was hardened with pride, he was deposed from his royal throne, and his glory was taken from him.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
God gave Nebuchadnezzar power and honor.
Nebuchadnezzar became proud in his heart.
His spirit became stubborn with pride.
God removed Nebuchadnezzar from his royal throne.
God took away Nebuchadnezzar’s glory.
passages.original: וּכְדִי֙ רִ֣ם לִבְבֵ֔הּ וְרוּחֵ֖הּ תִּֽקְפַ֣ת לַהֲזָדָ֑ה הָנְחַת֙ מִן־ כָּרְסֵ֣א מַלְכוּתֵ֔הּ וִֽיקָרָ֖ה הֶעְדִּ֥יוּ מִנֵּֽהּ׃

passages.text: He was driven away from mankind, and his mind was like that of a beast. He lived with the wild donkeys and ate grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven until he acknowledged that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of mankind, setting over it whom He wishes.
passages.sermon:
God punished King Nebuchadnezzar for his pride.
God drove Nebuchadnezzar away from other people.
Nebuchadnezzar no longer lived with humans.
His mind became like the mind of an animal.
He lived among wild donkeys.
He made his home with the animals.
He ate grass like an ox.
The dew from heaven soaked his body.
This lasted for a long time.
It continued until Nebuchadnezzar understood something important.
He learned that the Most High God rules over the kingdoms of people.
God gives power to anyone He chooses.
passages.original: וּמִן־ בְּנֵי֩ אֲנָשָׁ֨א טְרִ֜יד וְלִבְבֵ֣הּ׀ עִם־ חֵיוְתָ֣א שְׁוִי וְעִם־ עֲרָֽדַיָּא֙ מְדוֹרֵ֔הּ עִשְׂבָּ֤א כְתוֹרִין֙ יְטַ֣עֲמוּנֵּ֔הּ וּמִטַּ֥ל שְׁמַיָּ֖א גִּשְׁמֵ֣הּ יִצְטַבַּ֑ע עַ֣ד דִּֽי־ יְדַ֗ע דִּֽי־ שַׁלִּ֞יט אֱלָהָ֤א עִלָּיָא בְּמַלְכ֣וּת אֲנָשָׁ֔א וּלְמַן־ דִּ֥י יִצְבֵּ֖ה יְהָקֵ֥ים עֲלַיֵהּ׃

passages.text: But you his son, O Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, even though you knew all this.
passages.sermon:
Belshazzar was Nebuchadnezzar’s son.
Belshazzar knew what happened to his father.
Belshazzar did not humble his heart.
Belshazzar knew all these things.
Belshazzar still refused to humble himself.
passages.original: וְאַנְתָּה בְּרֵהּ֙ בֵּלְשַׁאצַּ֔ר לָ֥א הַשְׁפֵּ֖לְתְּ לִבְבָ֑ךְ כָּל־ קֳבֵ֕ל דִּ֥י כָל־ דְּנָ֖ה יְדַֽעְתָּ׃

passages.text: Instead, you have exalted yourself against the Lord of heaven. The vessels from His house were brought to you, and as you drank wine from them with your nobles, wives, and concubines, you praised your gods of silver and gold, bronze and iron, wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or understand. But you have failed to glorify the God who holds in His hand your very breath and all your ways.
passages.sermon:
Belshazzar was the king of Babylon.
Belshazzar exalted himself against the Lord of heaven.
People brought the vessels from God's house to Belshazzar.
Belshazzar drank wine from these vessels.
His nobles, wives, and concubines drank with him.
Belshazzar praised gods of silver and gold.
He praised gods of bronze and iron.
He praised gods of wood and stone.
These gods cannot see.
These gods cannot hear.
These gods cannot understand.
Belshazzar did not honor the true God.
The true God holds Belshazzar’s breath in His hand.
The true God controls all Belshazzar’s ways.
Belshazzar failed to glorify this God.
passages.original: וְעַ֣ל מָרֵֽא־ שְׁמַיָּ֣א׀ הִתְרוֹמַ֡מְתָּ וּלְמָֽאנַיָּ֨א דִֽי־ בַיְתֵ֜הּ הַיְתִ֣יו קָדָמַיִךְ וְאַנְתָּה וְרַבְרְבָנַיִךְ שֵֽׁגְלָתָ֣ךְ וּלְחֵנָתָךְ֮ חַמְרָא֮ שָׁתַ֣יִן בְּהוֹן֒ וְלֵֽאלָהֵ֣י כַסְפָּֽא־ וְ֠דַהֲבָא נְחָשָׁ֨א פַרְזְלָ֜א אָעָ֣א וְאַבְנָ֗א דִּ֠י לָֽא־ חָזַ֧יִן וְלָא־ שָׁמְעִ֛ין וְלָ֥א יָדְעִ֖ין שַׁבַּ֑חְתָּ וְלֵֽאלָהָ֞א דִּֽי־ נִשְׁמְתָ֥ךְ בִּידֵ֛הּ וְכָל־ אֹרְחָתָ֥ךְ לֵ֖הּ לָ֥א הַדַּֽרְתָּ׃

passages.text: Therefore He sent the hand that wrote the inscription.
passages.sermon:
God saw Belshazzar’s pride and sin.
God decided to act.
God sent a hand from His presence.
The hand wrote an inscription on the wall.
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֙יִן֙ מִן־ קֳדָמ֔וֹהִי שְׁלִ֖יַחַ פַּסָּ֣א דִֽי־ יְדָ֑א וּכְתָבָ֥א דְנָ֖ה רְשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: Now this is the inscription that was written: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN.
passages.sermon:
Daniel spoke to King Belshazzar.
Daniel explained the writing on the wall.
The inscription was clear and visible.
The words were: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN.
passages.original: וּדְנָ֥ה כְתָבָ֖א דִּ֣י רְשִׁ֑ים מְנֵ֥א מְנֵ֖א תְּקֵ֥ל וּפַרְסִֽין׃

passages.text: And this is the interpretation of the message: MENE means that God has numbered the days of your reign and brought it to an end.
passages.sermon:
Daniel spoke to King Belshazzar.
Daniel explained the meaning of the message.
Daniel said, “MENE means this.
God has counted the days of your kingdom.
God has finished your reign.
Your rule will end.”
passages.original: דְּנָ֖ה פְּשַֽׁר־ מִלְּתָ֑א מְנֵ֕א מְנָֽה־ אֱלָהָ֥א מַלְכוּתָ֖ךְ וְהַשְׁלְמַֽהּ׃

passages.text: TEKEL means that you have been weighed on the scales and found deficient.
passages.sermon:
Daniel spoke to King Belshazzar.
Daniel explained the meaning of the word "TEKEL."
God weighed you on the scales.
God found you lacking.
You did not measure up to God's standard.
passages.original: תְּקֵ֑ל תְּקִ֥ילְתָּה בְמֹֽאזַנְיָ֖א וְהִשְׁתְּכַ֥חַתְּ חַסִּֽיר׃

passages.text: PERES means that your kingdom has been divided and given over to the Medes and Persians.”
passages.sermon:
Peres is a word from God.
Peres means division.
God has divided your kingdom.
God has given your kingdom to the Medes.
God has given your kingdom to the Persians.
passages.original: פְּרֵ֑ס פְּרִיסַת֙ מַלְכוּתָ֔ךְ וִיהִיבַ֖ת לְמָדַ֥י וּפָרָֽס׃

passages.text: Then Belshazzar gave the command, and they clothed Daniel in purple, placed a gold chain around his neck, and proclaimed him the third highest ruler in the kingdom.
passages.sermon:
Belshazzar was the king of the Chaldeans.
Belshazzar gave a command.
The servants clothed Daniel in purple.
They placed a gold chain around Daniel’s neck.
They proclaimed Daniel as the third highest ruler in the kingdom.
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֣יִן׀ אֲמַ֣ר בֵּלְשַׁאצַּ֗ר וְהַלְבִּ֤ישׁוּ לְדָֽנִיֵּאל֙ אַרְגְּוָנָ֔א וְהַמּוֹנְכָא דִֽי־ דַהֲבָ֖א עַֽל־ צַוְּארֵ֑הּ וְהַכְרִ֣זֽוּ עֲל֔וֹהִי דִּֽי־ לֶהֱוֵ֥א שַׁלִּ֛יט תַּלְתָּ֖א בְּמַלְכוּתָֽא׃

passages.text: That very night Belshazzar king of the Chaldeans was slain, and Darius the Mede received the kingdom at the age of sixty-two.
passages.sermon:
Belshazzar was king of the Chaldeans.
That very night, someone killed Belshazzar.
Darius was a Mede.
Darius received the kingdom.
Darius was sixty-two years old.
passages.original: בֵּ֚הּ בְּלֵ֣ילְיָ֔א קְטִ֕יל בֵּלְאשַׁצַּ֖ר מַלְכָּ֥א כַשְׂדָּיָא׃פ וְדָרְיָ֙וֶשׁ֙ מָֽדָיאָ֔ קַבֵּ֖ל מַלְכוּתָ֑א כְּבַ֥ר שְׁנִ֖ין שִׁתִּ֥ין וְתַרְתֵּֽין׃
